articles.title: Install the launcher
articles.keywords: installation mac windows linux setup download architecture
articles.body: Download the build for your OS and CPU. Windows uses Setup.exe and offers install location, startup and shortcuts. On macOS drag the app from its DMG to Applications. On Linux make the AppImage executable; if FUSE is unavailable use --appimage-extract-and-run. Launcher OS support is separate from the apps in its library. See Launcher-KB2 and Launcher-KB12.

articles.title: Install and update applications
articles.keywords: apps update install location uninstall tray
articles.body: Use Install or Update in the library. Select an empty app folder and choose startup and desktop options. Updates check hashes before replacing files. Allow a running app to close before updating; force close is a separate choice. Uninstall can preserve or delete standard local data. External work folders are preserved. See Launcher-KB1 and Launcher-KB10. See Launcher-KB13 for coming-soon apps.

articles.title: Profile and social account suggestions
articles.keywords: profile mail socials accounts email passwords key
articles.body: Your optional profile stays on this device. Enter your name and one email address, then choose + Add email address for additional addresses, up to 20. Remove deletes a row; the first saved email is your primary suggestion. Choose profile photo accepts a PNG or JPEG smaller than 4 MB, crops it to a square and stores a small local PNG when you save. Remove photo restores your initial. Cancel discards unsaved profile and photo edits. Photos are not shared with providers or other apps. Optional social accounts hold usernames or public HTTPS profile URLs, never passwords or tokens. Shared profile suggestions do not sign in to provider accounts. Control overall, Mail and future social sharing separately. See Launcher-KB4, Launcher-KB10 and Launcher-KB16.

articles.title: TMApps sign in and app access
articles.keywords: sign in login otp email session linked authentication
articles.body: TMApps email-code sign-in requires the operator to deploy and configure the prepared sign-in service. Once enabled, sign in once and select which supported apps may request a TMApps session. This does not transfer social-network or mailbox passwords. Apps must implement the session handoff before they can reuse sign-in. Revoking app access stops future handoffs. See Launcher-KB3 and Launcher-KB10.

articles.title: Choose your appearance
articles.keywords: theme dark grey gray black orange colours color
articles.body: In Settings, choose the Appearance tab. Pick Orange, Grey or Black, move navigation to Left, Right, Top or Bottom, choose List or Grid, and toggle Compact Navigation Bar. Save keeps changes; Cancel restores the previous appearance. The title bar and scrollbars use the dark theme. Drag the title bar to move the window, double-click to maximize or restore, and use its window buttons to minimize or close. In list view, Details sits below the Open, Install or Update action. Spotify playback modes and account opens the music settings. See Launcher-KB9 and Launcher-KB15.

articles.title: Reduce resource usage
articles.keywords: performance cpu gpu ram memory network startup tray media
articles.body: Close-to-tray keeps the launcher in memory; use Quit to release it. Startup launch affects boot time. Startup update checks use network and some CPU briefly. App videos use network, RAM, decoding CPU and GPU while playing; playback starts only when requested. Screenshots load only in app details. Close details to release media. Functional and resource checks run in the release workflow. See Launcher-KB5 and Launcher-KB9. Optional Spotify controls refresh every 15 seconds only while their music window is open and visible. Closing it stops refresh work. Browser streaming uses the browser's CPU, RAM and network; Connect playback uses the selected Spotify device. See Launcher-KB15.

articles.title: Review and submit a crash report
articles.keywords: crash errors logs github report privacy
articles.body: The launcher prepares a local report with app version, OS, architecture and redacted error details. Review the full draft before choosing Upload to GitHub Issues. That opens the GitHub report form; you sign in and submit it there. Nothing is sent automatically. Remove anything you do not want public. Reports omit credentials and your saved profile. See Launcher-KB8 and Launcher-KB10.

articles.title: Get help and request changes
articles.keywords: help faq bug issue feature request support github
articles.body: Use Help to search this library, request a feature, report a reproducible bug, or report another issue. Each action opens its matching GitHub form. Choose the affected app and describe expected versus actual behaviour. Do not include passwords, keys, mail content or private project files. See Launcher-KB7.

articles.title: App details and galleries
articles.keywords: details versions new features changelog video screenshots gallery
articles.body: Click an app name or Details to open its showcase. The header shows the app icon, description, version and update date. Open, Install or Update is available when the app supports your operating system; GitHub opens its source branch. Published screenshots appear in a gallery with Previous, Next and thumbnail buttons, up to ten per app. A showcase video appears only when published and plays only when requested. Missing media stays unpublished. Feature cards and Latest release show available app information; preview limitations remain in the release notes. Close the screen to release media resources. In List view Details is below the main app action. See Launcher-KB2 and Launcher-KB6.

articles.title: Privacy and local data
articles.keywords: privacy data delete accounts passwords credentials sharing
articles.body: Profile suggestions and app preferences are local to your OS user. Sign-in sessions, when configured, are protected with the OS credential facility; Linux without a secure keyring keeps sessions in memory only. GitHub reports become public only after you submit them. Uninstall choices apply to the selected app; external projects are kept. See Launcher-KB3 and Launcher-KB7.

articles.title: Search settings and knowledge articles
articles.keywords: settings search keywords kb library toggle
articles.body: Settings groups options into Appearance, Startup and performance, Help and KB Library, and Downloads and storage on Windows. Choose a section button to focus its controls. Search settings searches all sections by keyword. Help has a dedicated Search KB Library field on Windows; Open KB Library and support opens the searchable library on macOS and Linux. Include KB articles in settings search can be disabled without removing Help. Enter a stable reference such as Launcher-KB6 to find the matching guide. See Launcher-KB5, Launcher-KB6 and Launcher-KB8.

articles.title: Troubleshoot platform compatibility
articles.keywords: macos mac linux windows fuse gatekeeper tray unsupported install
articles.body: Choose x64 for Intel/AMD and arm64 for Apple Silicon or ARM Linux. Do not install a Windows EXE on macOS or Linux. Only published matching app packages can be installed. macOS packages currently use ad-hoc signing and are not notarized; OS approval may be required. Linux tray support depends on the desktop. See Launcher-KB1 and Launcher-KB7.

articles.title: Coming soon applications
articles.keywords: libraries coming soon unavailable question mark source install version date order
articles.body: Coming soon means no installable package has been published. A source branch or app icon alone does not mean an app is ready to install. Check for updates to refresh verified availability. The OS badges show the platforms with actual published builds; a Windows app cannot be installed by the macOS or Linux launcher. Libraries and Finance 0.1.0 now have Windows development packages and their app icons. Their feature sets are incomplete; review Details and release notes before installing. SocialsManager stays immediately before Agent Office, which is always last and moves down when apps are added. Older launchers may need to update and restart before they can read an expanded app catalog. See Launcher-KB2 and Launcher-KB14.

articles.title: Install Libraries and Finance
articles.keywords: libraries finance windows install beta development notes budgets profile data privacy
articles.body: Choose Check updates to load the published app catalog. A GitHub source push alone is not an installable app update: a tested package, version and checksum must also be published. Libraries 0.2.0-dev.1 is an unsigned Windows development preview with offline document, checklist, spreadsheet, slide and PDF editors. Advanced format fidelity and performance work remain pending. The packaged editor test used about 896 MiB after exercising all editors; close unused editors and quit the app when finished. Export backups before updating from Libraries 0.1.0. The preview uses a separate roaming TMA-Libraries/library-v2 profile; legacy local TMApps/TMA-Libraries records remain untouched. Import a schema-1 workspace export inside Libraries to migrate; close the legacy app first. Launcher 1.14.2 only deletes the legacy Libraries data location when Delete local data is chosen; the new preview profile is retained and must be managed separately. Finance remains 0.1.0 with budgets, savings and a manual investment workspace. Both apps store records without app-level encryption. No provider key is entered in the launcher. No macOS or Linux package is advertised until matching verification is complete. See Launcher-KB2, Launcher-KB10 and Launcher-KB13.

articles.title: Spotify playback and browser streaming
articles.keywords: spotify music premium pkce connect browser playback streaming callback sign in device
articles.body: Open Spotify in navigation, or Spotify playback modes and account in Settings. Connect Spotify signs in through your browser using PKCE. Choose Spotify app / Connect device or Browser streaming with in-app controls. In browser mode, open the web player, sign in there and start a track. Audio streams in the browser; TMA controls the active Spotify device. Premium and developer-app user access are required. Each app authorizes separately. Finish one sign-in before starting another. The registered callback is http://127.0.0.1:43823/spotify/callback. Authorization stays encrypted locally; without a secure Linux keyring it stays in memory. Closing the music window stops its 15-second refresh. Disconnect removes local authorization; revoke provider access in Spotify if needed. A busy port, denied access, inactive device or rate limit has an actionable message. See Launcher-KB6 and Launcher-KB10. Companion-app Spotify changes are uploaded as source for their next releases; existing companion downloads are unchanged.

articles.title: Autofill profiles across TMA apps
articles.keywords: profile sync autofill name email avatar account icon share local identity
articles.body: Save your optional name and email addresses through the top-right profile icon. Autofill compatible TMA app profiles on this device enables shared suggestions; Mail and social metadata keep their additional sharing controls. Compatible apps read suggestions when opened or focused. Empty fields and previously imported values update automatically; app-specific edits and connected account identities are preserved. Office and Finance source updates add editable profile icons; their public downloads gain this with their next releases. Mail already supports launcher name/email suggestions on Windows. Profile sharing is local to the current OS user, not cloud sync or provider authentication. Disabling sharing stops future imports and keeps existing local app values. Credentials and app-specific keys are still entered in each provider app. See Launcher-KB3, Launcher-KB4 and Launcher-KB10. Earlier released Mail versions continue their existing display-name sync behavior until the companion update; connected email identities stay protected.

articles.title: Check service status
articles.keywords: service status API checker red green network github spotify microsoft google health connection
articles.body: Open Service Status and choose Check APIs now. API Checkers group the suite public service checks by app. Gray means not checked. Glowing green means the public endpoint responded; glowing red means unavailable from this device or rate-limited. Checks send no account credentials and do not run in the background. Green is not proof that an account is signed in, a subscription is active or permissions are granted. Microsoft and Google sign-in discovery and GitHub and Spotify endpoint reachability are covered; additional app-specific providers and IMAP/SMTP account tests remain inside their apps. Companion Spotify integration reaches downloads in their own releases. Retry after checking your connection if a service is red. See Launcher-KB7, Launcher-KB8 and Launcher-KB15.

tma-mail.releaseNotes:
# TMA-Mail changelog

Development history reconstructed from the local prototype milestones. Earlier versions were local builds, not previously published GitHub releases.

## 0.16.5 beta — 19 October 2026

- Replace stretched notification lettering with the heavier Segoe UI Black weight. Scale uniformly to preserve the natural digit proportions while keeping the count centred inside the red bubble.
- Visually verify single digits, two digits and `99+` at full and taskbar sizes; pass the existing notification integration checks.

## 0.16.4 beta — 19 October 2026

- Correct the remaining small `99+` notification text by fitting the glyph height independently of its width. Use narrower lettering for large counts so it remains tall inside the circular badge.
- Verify the `99+` white lettering occupies ten pixels vertically at a 16px taskbar size, compared with six in 0.16.3. Pass the existing 120 workspace-suite checks.

## 0.16.3 beta — 19 October 2026

- Enlarge the white unread notification count for single digits, two digits and `99+`. Centre the visible glyphs rather than the font's line-height box so the text fills the red bubble more evenly.
- Verify rendered badges at full and taskbar sizes; pass the existing 120 workspace-suite checks, including notification count and Appearance toggle behavior.

## 0.16.2 beta — 19 October 2026

- Hide deleted messages immediately, including bulk deletes and deletes queued behind sync or another mail operation. Complete the server move in the background, preserving original cached folders and UIDs until confirmation. Keep pending deletions hidden if a refresh replaces cached message objects.
- Update visible Inbox unread counts and the notification badge while deletion is pending. Restore messages and counts if the server rejects the delete or the account disconnects before the operation starts. Retain the existing duplicate-operation guard and server-identity handling.
- Move local message persistence off the immediate toolbar and pop-out action path so local deletes update the view before saving to disk.
- Use the same responsive toolbar layout and green buttons in separate email windows, including all main actions, the divider, Fast Functions, Create New Button and Edit Bar. Synchronize saved action/Fast Function ordering and edit mode between windows. Keep actions, recipient history and custom buttons tied to the opened message's mailbox rather than the main selection.
- Double-click a separate window's subject to edit it in a themed Save/Cancel dialog. Validate a single-line subject, update the main list and window title, and retain the local edit through sync and encrypted cache reload. The original server subject is unchanged.
- Add 11 synthetic checks for immediate visibility, slow-server behavior, bulk deletion, account isolation, refresh persistence, confirmation and failure recovery. No real mail was deleted by automated tests.
- Add 12 separate-window toolbar/editor checks and three edited-subject persistence/search checks.

## 0.16.1 beta — 19 October 2026

- Prevent `Unknown Mailbox: [Gmail]` sync failures by excluding Gmail's reserved system-label parent containers, non-selectable folders and nonexistent placeholders before sending STATUS or EXAMINE. Preserve the folder hierarchy and sync real children, including All Mail. Apply the same folder eligibility check to subscription scans.
- Wait five minutes after each account's completed sync before its next fallback scan; retry failed attempts after one minute. Keep new-mail monitoring, explicit Sync, resume and action-triggered refreshes immediate. Avoid duplicate scheduled work already queued for an account.
- Add 10 in-memory IMAP protocol checks for container handling, child-folder sync, cached message preservation, server failures and cancellation, plus six scheduling checks. Automated checks use synthetic data and do not access real mailboxes.

## 0.16.0 beta — 18 October 2026

- Suggest recipient addresses while typing in To, Cc or Bcc for new messages, replies, forwards and Fast Functions. Rank valid addresses from the composing account's cached sent mail by message frequency, then recency; omit the account itself, duplicates, drafts and unrelated accounts. Support arrows, Enter/Tab, Escape and mouse selection, preserving other recipients.
- Queue Delete, Archive and Move behind active mail operations instead of refusing clicks during sync. Cancel an active sync to let queued moves proceed, then resume background work where appropriate. Keep manually paused mailboxes paused and reject duplicate moves or moves queued for disconnected accounts.
- Refresh source and destination cache entries after successful moves using the server's destination UID mapping. On servers without a mapping, refresh the destination on the next sync. Failed moves keep the cached source visible and do not automatically retry.
- Recognize common Deleted Items/Deleted Messages folder names and Gmail's All Mail archive when special-folder flags are unavailable. Keep pop-out reply recipient history tied to its original account after mailbox switching.
- Add 14 synthetic recipient/dropdown checks and 11 toolbar/move/account-isolation checks. No real mailbox was modified by automated tests.

## 0.15.9 beta — 18 October 2026

- Add per-mailbox Pause sync / Resume sync controls in the footer and Settings → Accounts. Pause stops queued/periodic sync and new-mail monitoring for that mailbox until resumed or the app restarts.
- Pause immediately when removal is selected. Cancelling the confirmation restores syncing unless the mailbox was already paused; confirming waits asynchronously for sync cancellation and the mail-operation lock before removing credentials. Reconnect-dialog disconnection also awaits removal.
- Pass cancellation through IMAP/SMTP authentication and modern OAuth token renewal, suppress late sync callbacks, retain completed cache batches and preserve other accounts and encrypted caches.
- Add eight synthetic workspace checks for cancellation, removal ordering, queue isolation, cache retention and resume controls. No real mailbox is removed during tests.

## 0.15.8 beta — 17 October 2026

- Add a green question-mark help button beside the Google app-password option and password field. Hover shows 'How to get app specific password?'; clicking opens Google's official app-password guide.

## 0.15.7 beta — 17 October 2026

- Keep Google desktop OAuth configuration local and preserve the Google app-specific password option. Public packaging uses only the public provider configuration and refuses a nonempty Google OAuth client secret.
- Add a provider setup regression confirming that Google browser sign-in and password setup are both available and that password setup keeps password authentication.
- Google sign-in initially requires a listed test account. Production availability and any required Google verification remain separate provider setup steps.

## 0.15.6 beta — 17 October 2026

- Fix a reproduced MSAL json_parse_failed error while parsing valid Microsoft client-info JSON. The packaged JSON encoder version differs from MSAL's requested assembly version; redirect it to the shipped version, together with the async interfaces and task extensions dependencies.
- Add runtime regressions that exercise MSAL client-info parsing, token-response JSON, account-cache loading and cache roundtrip with synthetic data. The previous configuration reproduces the loader failure; the corrected configuration passes.
- Keep the safe Outlook diagnostics available. Live Microsoft sign-in and mailbox connection still require an account-holder retry.

## 0.15.5 beta — 17 October 2026

- Show MSAL/Microsoft error codes and a connection-details button for Outlook failures after browser authentication. Distinguish the browser/token step from session renewal during mailbox connection.
- Include only diagnostic identifiers, stage, HTTP status and targeted hints; omit raw Microsoft messages, token responses and callback URLs. Keep failed setup open for review/retry without adding an incomplete account.
- Add a synthetic post-authentication failure regression that verifies actionable error codes and excludes fake token/callback values. The reported live failure still requires its actual error code for a confirmed fix.

## 0.15.4 beta — 17 October 2026

- Bundle TMA-Mail’s Microsoft public client ID so Outlook setup offers Continue with Outlook and uses the existing MSAL system-browser sign-in flow. Register the desktop localhost redirect and delegated IMAP, SMTP and calendar permissions; users consent to their own account access.
- Source builds use the tracked public client configuration unless a local provider-settings.json override exists. No Microsoft client secret is required; Gmail remains unconfigured.
- Verify the release configuration exposes Outlook sign-in without opening a browser or accessing a real mailbox. Live sign-in/consent and organization-specific restrictions remain to be verified by the account holder.

## 0.15.3 beta — 17 October 2026

- Replace the white provider calendar discovery list with rounded green rows, readable names, checkboxes, and read-only/writable labels.
- Add selection counts, Select all, Clear selection, Add selected calendars, and Add all calendars. Connect and download multiple calendars together, then show All Calendars.
- Reconnecting known calendars preserves their cached events, pending uploads and uploaded-event identities. Save the group together and restore the previous list on save failure.
- Theme the reminder list and actions in green. Apply Dismiss/Snooze/Dismiss all immediately with selection-aware buttons, saved state, error rollback and visible confirmation.
- Add a Calendar reminder sound setting with seven cozy choices, None, Custom WAV and preview. Sound once per due reminder batch and again after snoozing; keep mail sound choices independent. Desktop calendar reminders use the existing bra

tma-agent-office.releaseNotes:
# Changelog

User-visible changes to Agent Office are recorded here. Entries under Unreleased
move into a numbered release when that release is prepared.

## Unreleased

## 0.2.0 — 2026-10-15

### Added

- Collapsible navigation ribbon with saved state, accessible labels, and tooltips.
- Open file location directly below a completed job's heading, using its saved directory.
- Claude Code CLI connection, account verification/sign-in, model selection, and per-agent provider selection for mixed teams.
- Live office appearance choices: Default (the original look), Robot workshop, and Neon network. Robot couriers deliver actual handoffs between desks and return to their stations.
- Office styles are shared by Overview and The Office Live; animations respect reduced motion and office pause, and restored history is not replayed.
- GitHub source repository setup and project instructions for maintaining this changelog.

### Validation

- 51 automated tests pass, including provider routing, ribbon persistence, completed-job folder access, and real-event/reduced-motion animation behavior.
- Claude integration is covered by protocol fixtures and a mixed-provider file-handoff test. A live Claude generation run requires an installed native CLI and signed-in Claude account.
- Office appearances and collapsed navigation were rendered in isolated Electron windows for visual checks; fixture jobs do not perform live AI work.

## 0.1.0 — 2026-10-15

### Added

- Windows desktop application with a visual agent office, Overview, and dedicated The Office Live tab.
- Configurable specialist agents, collaborative stage handoffs, job priorities, pause, cancellation, and retry.
- Eight project zones: Forge, Content, SNS, Products, Infra, Business, Games, and Archive; project status styling and seven-day inactivity indicators.
- Codex integration with ChatGPT browser sign-in, account model selection, usage information, and streamed output. No API key is required for this connection.
- Optional OpenAI API connection with encrypted Windows key storage or session-only credentials.
- ArtCraft integration for all 13 applications shown in the suite, including per-agent app permissions, folder confinement where supported, and action review.
- Spotify desktop playback information and previous/play/pause/next controls through Windows media sessions.
- Light, dark, and system appearance, reduced motion, and text scaling from 100% to 200%.
- Projects tab with live disk changes, nested folder navigation, safe text previews, recent changes, and Open folder.
- Per-project folder location and folder name controls, full-path preview, and persistent folder settings.
- Completed Jobs tab with saved deliverables, tool results, file locations, and history across restarts.
- Windows installer with installation-folder selection, Desktop and Start menu shortcuts, and uninstall support.

### Fixed

- Corrected the Codex project configuration that described writable work as read-only and caused chat-only output instead of saved files.
- Jobs now verify that non-empty output files were created or changed before reporting completion. Empty folders, unchanged files, and chat claims do not pass verification.
- Generated Codex images are copied into the project instead of being left only in the runtime cache.
- Specialist stages are coordinated by Agent Office; unnecessary internal delegation is discouraged, and the tool budget scales with the team.
- Linked jobs and supported ArtCraft sessions use the selected project directory, including locations outside the office default workspace.
- Project folder names reject invalid Windows characters and reserved names; existing folders are not overwritten or silently moved.
- Interrupted jobs are reported as failures and are never automatically retried. Explicit retry preserves the original job history.

### Validation

- 42 automated tests pass for the current implementation.
- Real signed-in Codex checks created and read back HTML, and completed a two-specialist job producing five SVG logos, a gallery, a README, and review notes.
- A real VectorCraft open/export check verified output in a custom project folder. Automated protocol fixtures do not themselves constitute live AI generation tests.

# TMA-Libraries version notes

## 0.2.0-dev.1 — 22 October 2026

Electron desktop rebuild with a brown Finance-inspired shell, tabs and ten document choices. Adds transactional SQLite storage, legacy migration, assets/revisions, native copies, Trash/Restore and confirmed permanent deletion, rich-document templates, Books, spreadsheets, slides and PDF tools. Settings include search, support drafts, offline help, accessibility choices, autosave and templates.

Storage, representative format adapters and desktop workflows are checked; PDF redaction is independently checked. This is a development preview: full Office fidelity, complete editor tooling, memory targets, accessibility/standards, Word KB publication, Launcher and cross-platform distribution remain open. See VERIFICATION-0.2.0.md. Legacy source is retained for migration/reference.

## 0.1.0 — 21 October 2026

Initial Windows desktop foundation using Windows Forms and .NET Framework 4.8, with no required paid services or external packages.

- Offline plain-text notes, checklists, optional completion progress and side notes.
- Folders, favourites, recent documents, search and coloured tags.
- Atomic local saves, previous-save recovery and native workspace import/export.
- Autosave defaults to five seconds when changed; configurable from two to 300 seconds or disabled.
- First-run setup offers optional larger text/high contrast, both off by default. Feature tour can be replayed from the toolbar.
- Light, Grey and Black appearance; fixed keyboard shortcuts and Settings release notes.
- Leather Brown identity and white-folder executable/window icon.
- Word KB draft with setup, offline operation, recovery, error catalogue and performance guidance. Rendering, master KB linking and publication are pending.

Advanced editors and the other pending specification items are not included. No Launcher package, remote publication, encryption, sync, tray, connection indicator or support forms are claimed.

tma-finance.releaseNotes: TMA-Finance 0.1.0 Windows development build. Budgets, expenses, subscriptions, savings, exports and a manual USD investment workspace. Optional Finnhub requests require the user's provider key and permissions. Bank linking, cloud sync, background alerts, macOS/Linux builds and the full suite settings/help features are not complete.
